current_evidence: The council's 'How to apply for planning permission' page links 'Local Validation Requirements' (local-validation-list.docx) as the local validation list, separate from the per-type checklists. Grokbot's extract of that docx cites adopted Local Plan policies LP33/LP34, so it postdates the 2015 checklist. The copy of local-validation-list.docx the user uploaded is headed 'Wakefield Council Local Validation List September 2026' (month only, so the date is given as 2026-09-01).

issues.detail: The workbook links the 'Full and outline applications' validation checklist PDF, a short per-type checklist from 2015. The council's local validation list is a separate document, local-validation-list.docx ('Wakefield Council Local Validation List'). Grokbot read the docx but did not use it as the reference link.
issues.evidence: Uploaded docx heading: 'Wakefield Council Local Validation List September 2026'; workbook URL .../validation-checklist-full-outline-applications.pdf

issues.detail: The list date 2015-12-01 comes from the checklist PDF's CreationDate metadata. The local validation list itself is dated September 2026 in its heading, so the list date is almost 11 years out and the 'Outdated (>2y)? Yes' flag is wrong.
issues.evidence: 'Wakefield Council Local Validation List September 2026'; Date basis 'PDF metadata CreationDate'

issues.detail: Crime and Safety Assessment is missing from every sheet except a bare 'Crime Impact Statement' name on the s73 sheet, taken from the 2015 checklist. The list requires it for all applications. New or refurbished nightclubs, public houses, restaurants, cafes, bars and music venues also need a statement on keeping the premises safe and secure.
issues.evidence: Crime and Safety Assessment - 'When is it required? All applications.'

issues.detail: Flood Risk Information has no Full planning or Householder row. The list requires a Flood Risk Assessment, Sequential Test and Exception Test where Local Plan or national policy and guidance require them. Householder schemes need a Householder Flood Risk Assessment using the council's questionnaire template. Grokbot has only bare s73 names from the 2015 checklist ('Flood Risk Assessment + Run Off Impact Assessment', 'Flood Risk Sequential Test Evidence').
issues.evidence: Flood Risk Information and Assessments - 'Householder Flood Risk Assessment, a template is available...flood-risk-assessment-questionaire.docx'

issues.detail: Affordable Housing Information is not captured. Every major application that includes housing must give details of the affordable housing provision. This includes a plan showing each affordable home with its type and tenure.
issues.evidence: Affordable Housing Information - 'Every major application which includes the provision of housing must be accompanied by details of the proposed Affordable Housing provision.'

issues.detail: Three housing requirements are missing. (1) Housing Information: all applications for one or more new dwellings, including changes of use, must address Policies SP6, SP7, SP8, LP2 and LP3. (2) Accessible Housing: applications that provide accessible homes, or meet the policy thresholds for them, need details and a plan of the accessible homes by type. (3) Space Standards Statement: where the Nationally Described Space Standard applies, a statement must give bedrooms, bedspaces, gross internal area, bedroom widths and storage for each dwelling. Grokbot's 'Housing mix / dwelling standards' row covers only the floor-plan labelling rules.
issues.evidence: Housing Information - 'All applications which involve the provision of one or more new dwellings (including changes of use)'; Accessible Housing; Space Standards

issues.detail: The Wakefield District Design Code Checklist is not captured. The list says the application must include a Design Code Checklist and enough information to show compliance with the Design Code. Grokbot's 'Design Code / Masterplan / Parameter plans' row carries only the Masterplan text.
issues.evidence: Wakefield District Design Code - 'The application must be accompanied by sufficient information and a Design Code Checklist'

issues.detail: Several local BNG items are missing. Major development: GIS shapefiles for pre- and post-development habitats, a Preliminary Ecological Appraisal, and an Ecological Impact Assessment where habitat impact is substantial. Where significant on-site gain is proposed, a draft Biodiversity Gain Plan, Condition Assessment and draft 30-year Habitat Management and Monitoring Plan are also needed. Minor development: at least an Initial Biodiversity Statement showing 10% gain, the Statutory or Small Sites Metric and a habitat plan. Anyone claiming an exemption must submit the Exemption Declaration Form.
issues.evidence: BNG - 'Local Validation Requirements for Minor Development'; 'A completed Exemption Declaration Form will be required for applications where an exemption...is being claimed'

issues.detail: The thresholds in the Environmental, Energy and Sustainability Statement are missing. An Energy Assessment (LP32) is needed for sites of 0.5 ha or more, 10 or more dwellings, or 1,000 sqm or more of employment, commercial, leisure or community floorspace, conversions included. Non-residential development over 1,000 sqm needs BREEAM Excellent evidence (LP33). District heating and cooling details are needed where LP36 applies. Grokbot's Energy row gives only the general policy sentence.
issues.evidence: 'All developments of 0.5 hectares or more in site area, or 10 or more dwellings, or 1,000 square metres or more floor area...must be accompanied by an Energy Assessment'

issues.detail: Green Belt Information is not captured. Applications in the Green Belt need details of compensatory improvements under SP22 or the site allocation. Extensions and replacement buildings also need volume and footprint calculations for the existing and proposed buildings, including any previous enlargements. This also applies to householder extensions.
issues.evidence: Green Belt Information - 'Calculations showing the volume and footprint of the proposed building(s) and of the existing building(s)'

issues.detail: Road Safety Audit is not captured, apart from a fragment of the words inside the Parking row's trigger. A Stage 1 Road Safety Audit is required for applications that connect to an existing highway or provide a new highway.
issues.evidence: Road Safety Audit - 'A Stage 1 Road Safety Audit is required for applications which include a connection to an existing highway and/or the provision of a new highway.'

issues.detail: Three requirements have no Full planning row and no trigger; they appear only as bare s73 names from the 2015 checklist. Landscaping Information is needed for all applications with new or changed landscaping. Open Space Impact Assessment is needed for development of existing open space (LP46). Utilities Information is needed for all applications where Local Plan Policy SP9 applies.
issues.evidence: Landscaping Information; Open Space Impact Assessment - 'development of an existing area of open space'; Utilities Information - 'all applications to which Local Plan Policy SP9 applies'

issues.detail: Two LP67 requirements are missing. A Water Impact Assessment is needed for all applications that could cause water pollution, including during construction or demolition. A general Pollution Impact Assessment is needed for developments likely to cause pollution or be exposed to it. Grokbot captured only the Air Quality part of the pollution section.
issues.evidence: Water Impact Assessment - 'must be submitted for all applications which have the potential to result in water pollution'; Pollution Assessment - 'In line with Local Plan Policy LP67'

issues.detail: The local plan and drawing rules are mostly missing. Location Plan: normally at 1:1250, with a red line taking in access, visibility splays, landscaping and parking, and a blue line around other land the applicant owns. Phasing Plan: required for all phased developments. Elevations: every elevation, for all operational development or external alterations (Grokbot files these only under Advertisement consent). Floor Plans: for new buildings, changes to existing buildings and changes of use. Sections: one for each house type where the Space Standard applies.
issues.evidence: Plans and Drawings - 'A Phasing Plan must be provided for all phased developments'; Location Plan - 'should normally be drawn at 1:1250 scale'

issues.detail: The Retail Impact Assessment is missing; only the Sequential Assessment is captured. An Impact Assessment is needed for retail and leisure proposals outside a defined centre that do not accord with the Local Plan. The thresholds are over 700 sqm gross external floorspace in sub-regional cities, principal towns and main towns, and over 300 sqm in District Centres and Local Retail Centres.
issues.evidence: Retail Impact and Sequential Assessments - 'Impact Assessment ... 700 square metres ... 300 square metres'

issues.detail: The minerals, hydrocarbons and waste requirements are missing. Minerals Extraction applications must address LP37. Non-minerals development on sites over 2 hectares must address LP38. Hydrocarbons exploration, appraisal or production must address LP39 and LP40. Waste applications must cover the Waste Application Requirements, such as distances to sensitive receptors, groundwater and geology.
issues.evidence: Minerals Details - 'Applications for non-minerals development on sites over 2 hectares'; Hydrocarbons Assessment; Waste Application Requirements

issues.detail: Three place-specific assessments are missing. Landmark Sites Assessment: landmark buildings and sites identified in LP19. Skylines and Strategic Views Assessment: development likely to affect the city skyline or strategic views of the spires and towers (LP17). Public Services Impact Statement: development catering for users of publicly provided support services, such as mental health, substance misuse or adult social care, must meet LP45 Part 2.
issues.evidence: Landmark Sites Assessment; Skylines and Strategic Views Assessment; Public Services Impact Statement - 'Part 2 of Policy LP45'

issues.detail: Three items with no stated trigger are not captured: Digital Infrastructure Details (Policy SP20), Skills and Employment Information covering the construction and operational phases, and Site Specific Requirements for allocated sites.
issues.evidence: Digital Infrastructure Details - 'with reference to the requirements of Local Plan Policy SP20'; Skills and Employment Information; Site Specific Requirements (Allocated Sites)

issues.detail: Two requirements that apply to all applications have triggers taken from other sections. 'Highways / access details' quotes the Location Plan red-line sentence ('public highway, visibility splays...'), but the list says Highways Details are needed for all applications. 'Waste / Refuse and recycling storage details' quotes the end of the Soil Resource Survey sentence, but the list says all applications must include a Waste Management Plan.
issues.evidence: Highways Details - 'When is it required? All applications.'; Waste Management Plan - 'All applications must be accompanied by a Waste Management Plan.'

issues.detail: The transport rows carry sentence fragments from the Parking section. Transport Assessment ('The information can be combined with a Transport Assessment...') should say: developments generating significant transport movement. Travel Plan ('Assessment and/or Travel Plan, where required') should say: significant vehicular movement, plus all major office development under LP22. Parking ('respect of Parking Provision and Road Safety Audits.') should say: applications that affect existing parking or servicing, or create a need for more. Cycle parking quotes only the larger-scheme content list.
issues.evidence: Travel Plan - 'Local Plan Policy LP22 requires that applications for major office development require the submission of a Travel Plan'

issues.detail: The ecology triggers are broken. The Ecological Survey row's trigger is the fragment 'habitats or protected species.' The real triggers are development on or near designated nature sites, affecting notable habitats, protected or notable species, or wildlife corridors. An Appropriate Ecological Assessment is also needed near the Denby Grange Colliery Ponds SAC, and bat reports in Bat Alert zones. 'Biodiversity Checklist / Questionnaire' is a misnamed Initial Biodiversity Statement, cut off mid-sentence, and leaves out that it applies to major development.
issues.evidence: Ecology Reports - 'in proximity to the Denby Grange Colliery Ponds Special Area of Conservation'; BNG - 'Additional local validation requirements for applications for major development'

issues.detail: 'Agricultural Land Classification / Soils' merges two requirements. Its trigger is the Soil Resource Survey sentence with the opening cut off ('development sites, a soil resources survey...'), which loses 'prior to any earthwork operations on new major development sites'. It also leaves out the Agricultural Land Assessment trigger: non-agricultural use or loss of land suitable for commercial agriculture.
issues.evidence: Agricultural Land Assessment - 'Applications which involve the non-agricultural use, or loss...of land suitable for commercial agricultural use'

issues.detail: The Archaeological Assessment trigger is the 'What is required?' text, not the trigger. The trigger is sites that include or affect heritage assets with archaeological interest. Separately, every application in the Pontefract Design Improvement Areas needs a desk-based assessment.
issues.evidence: Archaeological Assessment - 'all applications within the Design Improvement Areas identified in the Policies Map: Pontefract Inset Map'

issues.detail: The Landscape and Visual Impact Assessment trigger quotes the optional Cumulative LVIA sentence. The main trigger is all applications likely to have significant effects on landscape or visual amenity, judged by nature, size, location and duration.
issues.evidence: Visual Impact Assessment - 'All applications likely to result in significant effects on the landscape and/or visual amenity'

issues.detail: 'Planning Obligations / S106 draft Heads of Terms' quotes a viability fragment, which makes it look like a general requirement. The list asks for a draft S106 only where viability reduces contributions below policy. The Viability row's trigger is cut off ('be met, a viability assessment must be submitted.'). It should be: where the applicant argues exceptional circumstances under LP7. That also needs an electronic appraisal and agreement to pay for the council's review.
issues.evidence: Viability Information - 'Where an applicant wishes to make a case for an exceptional circumstance where policy requirements cannot be met'

issues.detail: The Full planning 'Design and Access Statement' row quotes the Masterplan sentence ('of the Design and Access Statement) must be provided for major new developments...'). The list sets no DAS trigger. The Householder, Outline, Listed building and s73 DAS rows are run-together checklist item lists ('Holding Certificate Design and Access Statement Location Plan ... The fee'), not triggers.
issues.evidence: Design Masterplan - 'A Masterplan Statement (which may be provided as part of the Design and Access Statement)'

issues.detail: Several triggers stop after the first criterion or carry stray text. Air Quality leaves out 'could itself result in an AQMA designation' and 'conflict with an air quality action plan'. Land Contamination leaves out radon and ground gas, suspected contamination and sensitive receptors. CIL Form leaves out new supermarkets, retail warehouses and other CIL-liable development. Coal Mining starts with a stray 'CIL liability' and leaves out the exemption statement. EV charging, water efficiency and site levels/sections are mid-sentence fragments.
issues.evidence: Coal Mining trigger 'CIL liability Coal Mining Risk Assessment...'; CIL - 'New Supermarkets; New Retail Warehouses'

issues.detail: The 28 Variation of condition rows are bare item names copied from the 2015 removal/variation checklist, such as 'Air Quality Assessment' and 'Coal Mining Risk Assessment'. None says when it applies. One even includes the checklist's date stamp ('Visual Impact Assessments 08.12.2015').
issues.evidence: trigger_excerpt 'Visual Impact Assessments 08.12.2015'

issues.detail: Householder has only one Design and Access Statement row, but many local requirements cover householder work. Some apply to all applications: Crime and Safety Assessment, Highways Details, Waste Management Plan. Others are householder-specific: the Householder Flood Risk Assessment template and the Design Code Checklist. Others apply where the trigger is met: Coal Mining Risk Assessment in the High Risk Area, Heritage Statement, Green Belt volume calculations for extensions, Arboricultural Impact Assessment, and block plan and elevations.
issues.evidence: Coal Mining Risk Assessment - 'with all planning applications within a Referral Area'; Crime and Safety Assessment - 'All applications.'

issues.detail: Outline has only a DAS row and Reserved matters is marked '(none)', but the list does not exclude them. Examples: Planning Statement and Health Impact Assessment for all major applications, Affordable Housing for major housing schemes, Masterplan and Phasing Plan for phased major sites, BNG local requirements for major development, and Statement of Community Involvement.
issues.evidence: Planning Statement - 'required for all applications which involve a departure from the development plan, and for all major applications'

issues.detail: Some requirements appear only under s73 or Listed building consent and are missing from Full planning, where the list applies them. Examples: Structural Survey (for conversions or demolition where structural matters arise), Flood Risk Assessment, Crime and Safety, Landscaping, Open Space and Utilities.
issues.evidence: Structural Survey - 'For applications (including those which involve conversion or demolition) where structural matters need to be considered.'

issues.detail: The 'Minerals & waste (county)' sheet says '(none)'. Wakefield is a unitary minerals and waste planning authority, and its list has requirements specific to minerals extraction (LP37), hydrocarbons (LP39/LP40) and waste applications. Its Statement of Community Involvement also names mineral extraction.
issues.evidence: Minerals Details - 'Applications relating to the extraction of minerals must be accompanied by information to address...LP37'

issues.detail: The s73 sheet comes from the superseded 2015 checklist, not the current list. It includes items the September 2026 list does not require, such as 'Daylight/Sunlight Assessment', 'Photographs/photomontages' and 'Run Off Impact Assessment', plus 'Environmental Statement', which is a national EIA matter.
issues.evidence: app_type_rows Variation of condition s73: 'Daylight/Sunlight Assessment', 'Photographs/photomontages'

issues.detail: Several Full planning rows reuse the same source sentence. Masterplan and DAS both quote the Masterplan sentence. Agricultural Land/Soils and Waste both quote the Soil Resource Survey sentence. Transport Assessment and Travel Plan both quote the same Parking sentence. Cycle parking and Parking both come from the Parking Provision section.
issues.evidence: Rows 'Design Code / Masterplan' and 'Design and Access Statement' both: 'must be provided for major new developments expected to be delivered by multiple developers'

issues.detail: Some rows are not requirements. 'Pre-application advice / engagement details' is the encouragement sentence at the end of the BNG section. The tab_items 'When making a planning application...See Checklists below', 'Application forms and checklists...' and the 5MB file-size note come from the web page and are signposting or process text, not list requirements. 'Scale Wherever possible...' starts with a stray heading fragment.
issues.evidence: 'Further information may be required, and early pre-application discussions are encouraged.'

summary: Grokbot's reference link and 2015-12-01 date belong to the 2015 full/outline checklist; the current list is the docx headed 'Local Validation List September 2026'. Grokbot captured about 30 of the list's roughly 55 local items, but many triggers are cut-off fragments borrowed from nearby sections. Several requirements are missing entirely, including some that apply to all or all major applications (Crime and Safety, Flood Risk, Affordable Housing, Design Code Checklist, Green Belt, Road Safety Audit, minerals/waste). The application-type mapping is weak: most items are inferred into Full planning, Householder, Outline and Reserved matters are near-empty, and the s73 sheet is bare 2015 checklist names.
